content.title: Paul Thomas Anderson would be 12th to win 3 Oscars for same movie
content.text: According to Gold Derby predictions, Paul Thomas Anderson is expected to accomplish a rare Oscars triple play for One Battle After Another. The acclaimed filmmaker is the front-runner to win Best Picture, Best Director, and Best Screenplay, and, if he pulls it off, he would become just the 12th filmmaker to accomplish the feat in the 98 years of Academy Awards. Inspired by Thomas Pynchon’s 1990 novel, Vineland, One Battle After Another follows Bob Ferguson (Leonardo DiCaprio), a washed-up former revolutionary suddenly forced back into action to rescue his daughter, Willa (Chase Infiniti), from a corrupt military official (Sean Penn). Anderson would join the following 11 multihyphenates who swept the awards for producing, directing, and writing the same movie: Billy Wilder — The Apartment (1960) Francis Ford Coppola — The Godfather Part II (1974) James L. Brooks — Terms of Endearment (1983) Peter Jackson — The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King (2003) Joel Coen and Ethan Coen — No Country for Old Men (2007) Alejandro González Iñárritu — Birdman (2014) Bong Joon Ho — Parasite (2019) Daniel Kwan and Daniel Scheinert — Everything Everywhere All at Once (2022) Sean Baker — Anora (2024) As you can see, during the classic studio era, the milestone was incredibly rare, with Wilder the only person to manage the trifecta, while Coppola was the first in the auteur era. Since 2000, however, the feat has become slightly more commonplace. PTA is trending towards the Academy Award history books: he has so far managed to win all three trophies from Critics Choice, Golden Globes, and BAFTA, in addition to prizes from the Producers Guild and Directors Guild. The Writers Guild will announce its winners on March 8 in New York (the Los Angeles ceremony was canceled due to a staff strike). Anderson has received 11 prior Oscar noms for producing, directing, and/or writing, but has never won. They were for 1997's Boogie Nights, 1999's Magnolia, 2007's There Will Be Blood, 2014's Inherent Vice, 2017's Phantom Thread, and 2021's Licorice Pizza. One Battle After Another is his seventh film to earn him at least one Oscar bid, and it's looking like the lucky one this time. If all goes according to plan, Anderson will go into the Dolby Theatre on Oscar night as a 14-time nominee, but leave as a three-time winner.
